title: Finite-presentation module, morphism and equality descent over arbitrary qcqs affine-transition limits
statement:
Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with affine transition morphisms $p_{ji}:S_j\to S_i$ for $j\geq i$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Assume every $S_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and let $S=\varprojlim_i S_i$ with projections $p_i$ be its scheme limit: $p_{ji}\circ p_j=p_i$ for $j\geq i$, and every compatible family $t_i:T\to S_i$ from a scheme $T$ factors uniquely as $t_i=p_i\circ t$ through a morphism $t:T\to S$. For sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], finite presentation means that every point has an open neighbourhood $U$ on which there is an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^m\to\mathcal O_U^n\to F|_U\to0$ for finite $m,n$. Use tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] throughout, identifying iterated pullbacks by its canonical composition isomorphisms. Then:
(1) Every finitely presented $\mathcal O_S$-module $F$ admits a finitely presented $\mathcal O_{S_i}$-module $F_i$ at some $i$, with $p_i^*F_i\cong F$.
(2) For any $i$, finitely presented $\mathcal O_{S_i}$-modules $F_i,G_i$ and a morphism $u:p_i^*F_i\to p_i^*G_i$, there are $j\geq i$ and $u_j:p_{ji}^*F_i\to p_{ji}^*G_i$ whose pullback to $S$ equals $u$ through the canonical composition isomorphisms.
(3) For any $i$, finitely presented $\mathcal O_{S_i}$-modules $F_i,G_i$ and morphisms $u_i,v_i:F_i\to G_i$ with $p_i^*u_i=p_i^*v_i$, there is $j\geq i$ such that $p_{ji}^*u_i=p_{ji}^*v_i$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fp-affine-limit-chart-models] to $F$, above any chosen starting index. Obtain a finite affine cover, actual pair/triple refinement covers, their restricted ring colimits, and local finitely presented quasi-coherent models $N_a$ with identifications $e_a$ to $F$. The same lemma supplies local models on the auxiliary charts; compatibility is not yet imposed.

Apply [lem-trf-fp-affine-limit-overlap-cocycle] to these $N_a,e_a$. At a later common stage its pair-chart maps have descended inverses satisfying both identity composites; they agree on refinement overlaps, glue to full-intersection isomorphisms, and satisfy every triple cocycle and repeated-index identity. Their limit pullbacks are exactly $e_b^{-1}e_a$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], the given finitely presented $F$ is quasi-coherent. The finite affine open cover is fpqc. By [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] these compatible local modules glue to $F_i$; its preservation/reflection clause gives finite presentation. The compatible $e_a$ give an isomorphism of descent data on $S$, hence the same equivalence glues $p_i^*F_i\cong F$. This proves (1).

For (2), choose a finite affine cover of the given $S_i$ and finite affine refinements of its pair intersections. Their inverse images cover every later stage. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-cone-affine-projections-opens] each restricted system has affine transitions and the required limit; [lem-weil-pbc-limit-global-sections-colimit] gives its ring colimit. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] the given modules have finitely presented sections on these charts. The equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] and [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections-bijective] identify the restrictions of $u$ with scalar-extended module maps. The map clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] lifts them to one stage; its equality clause makes the lifts agree on every pair refinement at a common later stage. Full faithfulness of [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] glues $u_j$ and verifies its pullback is $u$ through the canonical tensor composition comparisons.

For (3), use the same stage charts and section identifications as in Step 4. The equality clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] makes $u_i,v_i$ agree on each affine chart after one common upper bound. The inverse-image charts still cover that stage. Faithfulness of [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] gives the global equality.

lean.statement: theorem finitePresentation_descent_affineLimit {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) [∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, CompactSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map f)] (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) : (∀ F : c.pt.Modules, F.IsFinitePresentation → ∃ (i : I) (F_i : (D.obj (op i)).Modules), F_i.IsFinitePresentation ∧ Nonempty ((tensorPullback (c.π.app (op i))).obj F_i ≅ F)) ∧ (∀ (i : I) (F_i G_i : (D.obj (op i)).Modules), F_i.IsFinitePresentation → G_i.IsFinitePresentation → ∀ u : (tensorPullback (c.π.app (op i))).obj F_i ⟶ (tensorPullback (c.π.app (op i))).obj G_i, ∃ (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j) (u_j : (tensorPullback (D.map (homOfLE hij).op)).obj F_i ⟶ (tensorPullback (D.map (homOfLE hij).op)).obj G_i), (affineLimitTensorPullbackComparison D c hij F_i).inv ≫ (tensorPullback (c.π.app (op j))).map u_j ≫ (affineLimitTensorPullbackComparison D c hij G_i).hom = u) ∧ (∀ (i : I) (F_i G_i : (D.obj (op i)).Modules), F_i.IsFinitePresentation → G_i.IsFinitePresentation → ∀ u_i v_i : F_i ⟶ G_i, (tensorPullback (c.π.app (op i))).map u_i = (tensorPullback (c.π.app (op i))).map v_i → ∃ (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j), (tensorPullback (D.map (homOfLE hij).op)).map u_i = (tensorPullback (D.map (homOfLE hij).op)).map v_i)
